Proposed Resolution for Provost Donald DeHayes September 30, 2021 WHEREAS, Donald DeHayes was appointed as Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs at the University of Rhode Island in December 2007, and WHEREAS, Provost DeHayes had come to the University of Rhode Island after earning his Ph.D. at Michigan State University in Population Genetics of Forests, and went on to be a distinguished faculty member in the field o f forest ecology and Dean of the prestigious Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources at The University of Vermont (UVM), and WHEREAS, Provost DeHayes while serving as Provost instituted and institutionalized the practice of campus -community-wide January Academic Summits and creation of the Joint Committee on Academic Planning to develop a ‘grass-roots’ approach for Academic Planning at URI, and WHEREAS, Provost DeHayes developed and instituted the concept of J -term courses at URI that are popular with students, by keeping them on -track with their four-year academic plan and are often conducted in places far-away from Rhode Island’s unpredictable winter weather, and WHEREAS, over the years, Provost DeHayes greatly enhanced the prestige of the University in keeping with its Land Grant, Sea Grant and Urban Grant traditions of instruction, scholarship and community engagement, and promoting the study of health sciences and improved general education with big thinking and grand challenges at the University of Rhode Island, and WHEREAS, after fourteen faithful years of service to the University he has decided to hang up his forestry boots and relinquish his keys to the East Wing of Green Hall in exchange for a fishing pole.

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, The University of Rhode Island Faculty Senate extends its appreciation to Donald DeHayes for his innovation in his role as Provost and Vice President of Academic Affairs, and his dedication to and participation in shared governance with the Faculty Senate, and we wish him all the best in his future endeavors.
